summary: With the setPalette live-reference engine fix in place the original now renders, and the port is clearly the same pattern — a full-strip palette gradient sweeping back and forth while cross-fading between the same three palette families on the same ~7 s schedule — but the port's sweep is a linear triangle wave covering only 0.48 of the strip where the original's is a sine covering the whole strip (so ~2x too slow on average, with no easing at the turnarounds), and its palette hues are noticeably shifted/washier.
observations: RE-JUDGE CONTEXT: the original is no longer silent-null. rj-baseline (6 s, 20 fps, 60 px strip) gives orig meanBrightness avg 97.2 (min 74, max 101), motion avg 6.6, brightnessTrend steady, compileError/runtimeError null. The prior 'orig-unrenderable' verdict is superseded.

Both sides draw the same THING: a continuous colour ramp wrapped around the 60-px strip with one sharp discontinuity (a 'cliff' from the palette's bright end back to black), the whole ramp scrolling along the strip. Confirmed from --dump profiles, e.g. rj-dump-base t=0 orig brightness runs 110,117,...,225 at px24 then 0,0,0,0,0 at px25-29 and climbs again; port runs 1,4,...,249 at px59 with the cliff at the 59/0 wrap.

MOTION LAW — the headline divergence. Tracking the cliff index frame-by-frame and unwrapping (rj-dump-30s, 0.25 s spacing, 20 fps): ORIGINAL's velocity is a clean SINUSOID, peak +/-0.48 strip-widths/s, passing through exactly 0 at each turnaround; PORT's velocity is a perfect SQUARE wave — constant +/-0.153 strip-widths/s with instantaneous reversal (triangle-wave position). At 600 px the orig velocity series over one half-cycle reads -0.480,-0.453,-0.413,-0.333,-0.247,-0.147,-0.033,+0.087,...,+0.480,... while the port reads -0.153 repeated 12 times then +0.153 repeated 12 times.

SWEEP AMPLITUDE — the second half of the same divergence. Peak-to-peak excursion measured on four rigs (rj-px12 / rj-dump-30s(60px) / rj-px120 / rj-px600): original = 12/60/120/600 px = exactly 1.00 x strip length every time; port = 5/29/58/288 px = 0.42-0.48 x strip length. Both are therefore resolution-independent, but the port sweeps only about HALF the strip. The port's travel is also biased to one end: it oscillates between 0.51N and 0.99N and never visits the lower half of the strip's phase, whereas the original runs from -0.07N to +0.94N (i.e. it wraps).

PERIOD MATCHES. Turnarounds are at t = 3.25, 6.50, 9.75, 13.00, 16.25, 19.50 s on the port (exact, identical at 10/20/40 fps) and at t ~ 1.6, 4.87, 14.6, 18.0, 21.4, 24.6, 27.9 s on the original — half-period 3.25 s (port) vs 3.29 s (orig), i.e. ~1% apart. So the port is not 'slower in time'; it covers half the distance in the same time, giving mean speed 0.153 vs 0.303 strip/s (2.0x) and peak speed 0.153 vs 0.48 strip/s (3.1x).

PALETTE CROSS-FADE SCHEDULE MATCHES ALMOST EXACTLY. Rolling each frame to align its cliff (removing motion) and diffing consecutive rolled frames isolates palette change: both sides show elevated change (12-16 mean-abs units, vs 0.3-3.7 between fades) over the SAME windows — 5.25-7.00 s, 12.50-14.25 s, 19.50-21.25 s, 26.50-28.50 s. Fade duration ~1.75 s, cycle ~7.0 s, on both sides.

PALETTE SEQUENCE MATCHES. Over 240 s (rj-survey240) both sides rotate through the same three families in the same order, indefinitely: blue/magenta -> green/yellow -> red/yellow -> repeat. The 16x16 grid rhythm images (rj-grid16) show the two sides' palette-band boundaries landing at the same times.

PALETTE COLOURS ARE OFF. Hue histograms (30-deg bins, pixels with value>0.08) per family, orig vs port: BLUE family orig = 57% blue(240-270), 14% violet, 29% magenta, sat 0.92, val 0.83; port = 31% azure(210-240), 29% blue, 10% violet, 30% magenta, sat 0.84, val 0.76 — the port adds a cyan/azure leg the original has none of. GREEN family orig = 70% true green(120-150) + 26% red/orange(0-60); port = 45% green(90-120), 21% yellow-green, 33% orange — no true green above 120 deg and no red stop at all. RED family orig = 72% red + 28% orange; port = 66% red + 20% orange + 14% yellow(60-90).

PALETTE ENDPOINTS DIFFER. In the blue family the original's mid ramp is pure (0,0,B) with G exactly 0 and B pinned at 255 through the magenta section (e.g. px26-59 at t=2 s: 12,0,255 ... 255,169,255); the port carries a green tint through the blue leg (G rises to 37) and its magenta desaturates toward red (B falls 253 -> 195 across px23-43). In the red family at t=17 s the original tops out at (255,254,116) and holds 4 black pixels before the cliff; the port runs all the way to (255,255,251) and has no black pixels at all.

BRIGHTNESS: the port is consistently ~13% brighter. rj-late (--skip 300, 20 s) orig meanBrightness avg 74.0 (min 47) vs port 83.9 (min 52); over 240 s mean channel values orig R105.1/G49.7/B71.5 vs port R117.8/G68.1/B69.2 — the port's excess is almost entirely GREEN (+37%), consistent with the hue-arc shifts above.

MOTION STATS reflect the easing difference directly: at 20 fps orig motion avg 6.6 (max 13) vs port 4.2 (max 8), and orig posts 18-24 zero-motion frames per 400-frame window (the sine pauses at each turnaround) vs 0-4 for the port (which never stops). Orig motion series alternates a smooth 13->0->13 envelope; port's alternates a flat 2,7,2,7 pixel-quantisation pattern with no envelope.

NO FRAME-RATE COUPLING on either side: rendering at 10, 20 and 40 fps puts the port's turnarounds at identical absolute times (3.25/6.50/9.75/13.00/16.25/19.50 s) and the original's at 4.75-5.00 and 18.00 s in all three. Both are time-based.

BOTH SIDES ARE RESOLUTION-INDEPENDENT and index-driven: the excursion is a fixed fraction of the strip at 12/60/120/600 px, and on a 16x16 grid the per-column rhythm image is flat (no 2D structure) on both sides.

STEADY STATE IS FINE ON BOTH. rj-late (--skip 300, 20 s, 20 fps): orig mean 74.0 trend steady, port mean 83.9 trend steady, port zeroMotionFrames 0. Neither dies, freezes, or saturates out to t=320 s.
SEED-INDEPENDENT: seed 1234 (rj-seed1234) reproduces seed 1 to within a fraction of a count on every summary stat on both sides (orig 74.0 vs 74.4 mean, port 83.9 vs 84.1). No RNG-driven content.

CONTROL SURFACE: neither side exposes any settable control (meta.json controls: [] for both; --probe-controls reports '(no settable controls)' on both). No control-surface mismatch to report, and no dialed comparison is applicable.

Best-circular-shift residual between the two sides' frames at matched times never falls below ~14 mean-abs units per channel (typ. 15-20 in the red family, 22-26 in blue, ~28 in green), i.e. even after removing all position offset the colour ramps do not coincide.
feedback: PRIMARY FIX — sweep amplitude: the original scrolls the palette exactly ONE FULL STRIP LENGTH back and forth (measured as 1.00x the pixel count at 12, 60, 120 and 600 px); the port scrolls only 0.48x. Double the port's sweep excursion so the palette phase traverses the whole strip, and centre it: the original's cliff visits every pixel index (unwrapped range -0.07N .. +0.94N) while the port's stays in the top half (0.51N .. 0.99N).

PRIMARY FIX — easing: the original's scroll position is SINUSOIDAL (velocity a clean sine, peak 0.48 strip/s, momentarily zero at each turnaround), the port's is a LINEAR TRIANGLE (velocity a square wave, constant 0.153 strip/s, instantaneous reversal). Visually this is the difference between the original's curved, S-shaped waterfall trace and the port's hard-cornered chevrons — obvious in any side-by-side. Swap the port's triangle-wave position source for a sine-eased one. Do NOT change the period: half-period is 3.29 s (orig) vs 3.25 s (port) and already matches.

Do not touch the palette cross-fade timing — it is already right. Both sides fade over ~1.75 s windows centred at the same instants (5.25-7.0, 12.5-14.25, 19.5-21.25, 26.5-28.5 s) on a ~7.0 s cycle, and both rotate through the same three families in the same order (blue/magenta -> green/yellow -> red/yellow) out to 240 s.

COLOUR — blue family: the original's ramp is black -> pure blue (0,0,255, green channel exactly 0) -> pure magenta (255,0,255, blue pinned at 255) -> pink/white. The port instead starts in azure (31% of its lit pixels sit at hue 210-240 deg, which the original never produces), carries G up to ~37 through the blue leg, and lets B sag to 195 in the magenta leg. Saturate the blue and magenta stops and remove the cyan leg.

COLOUR — green family: the original's dominant hue is true green at 120-150 deg (70% of lit pixels) with a red/orange stop (26% at 0-60 deg). The port produces NO hue above 120 deg and no red at all — it reads chartreuse/olive (45% at 90-120, 21% at 60-90, 33% at 30-60). Rotate the green stop back toward 130-140 deg and restore the red end of that palette.

COLOUR — red family: closest of the three, but the port runs the top of the ramp all the way to white (255,255,251) whereas the original stops at (255,254,116) and, importantly, holds ~4 pixels of pure black immediately after the palette wrap. The port has zero black pixels there. Restoring the black plateau and clipping the white end would also close most of the overall brightness gap (port mean 84 vs orig 74) and the +37% green excess in the 240 s channel means.

Nothing else needs attention: both sides are time-based (no frame-rate coupling at 10/20/40 fps), resolution-independent (identical strip-fraction behaviour at 12/60/120/600 px and on a 16x16 grid), seed-independent, and steady out to t=320 s. Neither pattern exposes any control, so there are no dials to reconcile.
